name: Meridian Financial Constitution
description: An open constitution for regulated financial-technology software — payments, cards, ledger, lending, servicing and the models that decide — expressed as ordinary and absolute provisions in the sense of Chapter 5, Definition 1 of the Digital Judiciary programme. It is a superset of the thirty-seven provisions of the released Meridian Financial pack, whose text and absolute flags are reproduced unchanged. Provisions carry a status (in_force, deferred, advisory, readiness) and an origin (shipped, extension). A provision that is not in force may never be absolute. Seven findings against the shipped provisions — six of them the consequence of an instrument that moved after the pack was written — are filed as draft amendments rather than applied.
status_note: A deferred provision is enacted but not yet applicable; an advisory provision names suggested actions rather than obligations; a readiness provision states an architecture the firm must be able to meet when a suspended rule resumes, and has no live compliance date. None of the three may be marked absolute, and the build refuses a constitution in which one is.

authorities.disjointness: A1: the three classes are pairwise disjoint over the deployment lifetime.

standing_declaration.note: A9 first limb. This corpus declares that a party holds contest standing adverse to grants, namely the second-line compliance officer, so that the N-standing cases can exercise both postures. A deployment must replace this with its own fact.

provisions.family_title: Payment security, strong authentication and open banking
provisions.title: Strong customer authentication is applied to every remote electronic payment and every access to payment account information, with dynamic linking to the amount and the payee, and an exemption is taken only from the exhaustive list the technical standard allows
provisions.citation: PSD2, Dir. (EU) 2015/2366 Art. 97; Commission Delegated Reg. (EU) 2018/389 (RTS on SCA and common and secure communication), Arts. 4-5 (dynamic linking) and 10-20 (exemptions)
provisions.source_status: EU texts reusable under Decision 2011/833/EU. The exemption list in the RTS is exhaustive and is set by the Commission, not by the payment service provider; a firm may not invent an exemption or accept the risk of skipping authentication, which is what makes this a who-may-decide floor rather than a severity claim. The PSD3 Directive and Payment Services Regulation proposals were still in the legislative procedure at the last check and are not relied on here — directionally supported, not verified as of 6 September 2026.
provisions.risk_framework: 2.2 PSD2 SCA and the Instant Payments Regulation; APP-fraud reimbursement

provisions.family_title: Payment security, strong authentication and open banking
provisions.title: A credit transfer in euro is checked against the payee's name before the payer confirms it, the match result is shown to the payer, and no batch, bulk or retry path skips the check
provisions.citation: Instant Payments Regulation, Reg. (EU) 2024/886, inserting Art. 5c into Reg. (EU) 260/2012 (verification of payee), applicable from 9 October 2025
provisions.source_status: EU text reusable. Ordinary rather than absolute: the regulation gives the payer the right to be told of a mismatch and to proceed anyway, so the duty is to run the check and surface the result, not to block the payment — a duty whose implementation the firm may legitimately shape.
provisions.risk_framework: 2.2 PSD2 SCA and the Instant Payments Regulation; APP-fraud reimbursement

provisions.family_title: Payment security, strong authentication and open banking
provisions.title: Mandatory reimbursement of an authorised push-payment scam victim, its assessment window and its treatment of vulnerable customers are read from the regulator's direction and are never product settings
provisions.citation: UK Payment Systems Regulator, Faster Payments APP scams reimbursement requirement in force from 7 October 2024 (Policy Statement PS24/7; Specific Direction 20 for Faster Payments, Specific Direction 21 for CHAPS), made under the Financial Services (Banking Reform) Act 2013
provisions.source_status: UK regulatory material under Open Government Licence v3.0. Absolute because the reimbursement obligation, the maximum level and the claim-excess treatment are set by the regulator's direction; a product owner who tunes them is exercising a legislative power. Note the announced consolidation of the PSR into the FCA: the direction remains the operative instrument, but the naming of the issuing body is directionally supported, not verified as of 6 September 2026.
provisions.risk_framework: 2.2 PSD2 SCA and the Instant Payments Regulation; APP-fraud reimbursement

provisions.family_title: Payment security, strong authentication and open banking
provisions.title: A request for payment carries a verified sender, and an instant-rail transfer is fraud-scored before settlement with a recall path that survives a change to the rail integration
provisions.citation: The Clearing House RTP operating rules and FedNow Service operating procedures (identifiers only); Reg. E, 12 CFR §1005.11 for the consumer limb; Reg. (EU) 2024/886 Art. 5d on fraud-risk measures
provisions.source_status: Rail operating rules are cited by identifier and no text is reproduced; US regulation is public domain and EU text is reusable. Ordinary: the rails require fraud controls without prescribing their shape, so the firm's design is its own.
provisions.risk_framework: 2.2 PSD2 SCA and the Instant Payments Regulation; APP-fraud reimbursement

provisions.family_title: Fraud, identity theft, account takeover and applicant identity
provisions.title: The identity-theft prevention programme's red-flag rules run on every covered account and application, each detection has a documented response, and no channel is exempted by configuration
provisions.citation: FTC Red Flags Rule, 16 CFR §681.1 and Appendix A; SEC Reg. S-ID, 17 CFR §§248.201-248.202; FACT Act §114, 15 U.S.C. §1681m(e)
provisions.source_status: US regulation and statute, public domain. Ordinary because the rule requires a programme appropriate to the institution's size and risk and leaves the red flags themselves to the firm's identification.
provisions.risk_framework: 2.2 Red Flags / Reg S-ID; FFIEC authentication; FCRA permissible purpose

provisions.family_title: Fraud, identity theft, account takeover and applicant identity
provisions.title: High-risk actions — credential reset, payee addition, limit increase, address change — require a step-up challenge whose strength matches the risk, and no recovery path reintroduces a bypass
provisions.citation: FFIEC, Authentication and Access to Financial Institution Services and Systems (August 2021), superseding the 2005 and 2011 guidance (handbook title cited as a fact); GLBA Safeguards Rule, 16 CFR §314.4(c)(5)
provisions.source_status: US regulation public domain; the FFIEC guidance is cited by title. Ordinary: the 2021 guidance is expressly risk-based and does not mandate a specific control, so this is a firm control informed by supervisory expectation.
provisions.risk_framework: 2.2 Red Flags / Reg S-ID; FFIEC authentication; FCRA permissible purpose

provisions.family_title: Fraud, identity theft, account takeover and applicant identity
provisions.title: Applicant identity elements are verified against an authoritative source and scored for synthetic-identity indicators before an account is funded, including thin-file and no-file applicants
provisions.citation: 31 CFR §1020.220 (customer identification); Federal Reserve, Synthetic Identity Fraud in the U.S. Payment System (2019-2020 white-paper series) and the SSA electronic Consent Based Social Security Number Verification service, 42 U.S.C. §405(c)(2)(I)
provisions.source_status: US regulation and statute, public domain; the Federal Reserve papers are US Government works cited by title. Ordinary: no rule prescribes a synthetic-identity control, and MF-103 already carries the absolute CIP duty, so this provision states the firm's own detection duty without competing with it.
provisions.risk_framework: 2.2 Red Flags / Reg S-ID; FFIEC authentication; FCRA permissible purpose

provisions.family_title: Fraud, identity theft, account takeover and applicant identity
provisions.title: No consumer report is obtained or used without a permissible purpose recorded before the request, certified by the requesting role and specific to that request; no blanket or defaulted purpose is accepted
provisions.citation: FCRA, 15 U.S.C. §1681b(a) (permissible purposes) and §1681b(f) (prohibition on obtaining or using a report without one); §1681e(a) (user certification)
provisions.source_status: US statute, public domain. Absolute because §1681b(f) is a flat statutory prohibition carrying civil and, for knowing violations under §1681q, criminal liability; the permissible purposes are enumerated by Congress and no officer of the firm may add to them or accept the risk of proceeding without one.
provisions.risk_framework: 2.2 Red Flags / Reg S-ID; FFIEC authentication; FCRA permissible purpose

provisions.family_title: Fraud, identity theft, account takeover and applicant identity
provisions.title: An account for an applicant the record shows to be under eighteen is opened only with a verified adult custodian, and personal information is not collected online from a child under thirteen without verifiable parental consent
provisions.citation: COPPA, 15 U.S.C. §§6501-6506 and the FTC Children's Online Privacy Protection Rule, 16 CFR Part 312; state contract law on the infancy doctrine (e.g. Cal. Fam. Code §6710, disaffirmance)
provisions.source_status: US statute and regulation, public domain; state statute is an edict of government. COPPA reaches an online service directed to children or with actual knowledge it collects from an under-13, which a general-purpose banking product usually is not — the operative floor for opening and for payment obligations is state contract law, under which a minor may disaffirm. The 2025 amendments to Part 312 and their compliance date are directionally supported, not verified as of 6 September 2026.
provisions.risk_framework: 2.2 Red Flags / Reg S-ID; FFIEC authentication; FCRA permissible purpose

provisions.family_title: Consumer notices, electronic consent and communications
provisions.title: Before a disclosure the law requires in writing is delivered electronically instead of on paper, the consumer's informed consent is captured with the hardware and software statement, and the consent stays withdrawable
provisions.source_status: US statute, public domain. §7001(c) is a condition on using an electronic record to satisfy a writing requirement; it does not itself make any record a writing. Ordinary because the statute prescribes the consent's content, not the surface, and a defective consent is cured by re-consenting rather than by an irreversible harm.
provisions.risk_framework: 2.2 E-SIGN, TCPA, Reg P and Reg F; UDAAP communications

provisions.family_title: Consumer notices, electronic consent and communications
provisions.title: No autodialed call, prerecorded or artificial-voice message, or automated text reaches a wireless number without recorded prior express consent for that purpose, written where the purpose is marketing, and revocation is honoured on every channel
provisions.citation: TCPA, 47 U.S.C. §227(b)(1)(A); 47 CFR §64.1200(a)(1)-(3), (f)(9) (prior express written consent) and (a)(10) (revocation)
provisions.source_status: US statute and regulation, public domain. Verified 6 September 2026: the FCC's one-to-one-consent amendment was vacated by the Eleventh Circuit in January 2025 and is not relied on; the 2024 revocation rule is in force except the limb extending a revocation across all messages, whose effective date the FCC deferred — that deferral date is directionally supported, not verified. Kept ordinary rather than absolute because MF-401's UDAAP floor and the existing CP family already carry the consumer-facing absolutes, and a consent defect here is remediable.
provisions.risk_framework: 2.2 E-SIGN, TCPA, Reg P and Reg F; UDAAP communications

provisions.family_title: Consumer notices, electronic consent and communications
provisions.title: A privacy notice is delivered before nonpublic personal information is shared outside the exceptions, the opt-out reaches every disclosure path, and reliance on the annual-notice exception is checked against its conditions
provisions.citation: GLBA, 15 U.S.C. §6802-6803; Reg. P, 12 CFR §§1016.4 (initial notice), 1016.5 and 1016.5(e) (annual notice and its exception), 1016.7 (opt-out) and 1016.10 (limits on disclosure)
provisions.source_status: US statute and regulation, public domain. Ordinary: the sharing itself is lawful when the notice and opt-out are given, so the duty is procedural rather than prohibitory. Distinct from MF-308, which governs data reaching a model or a provider's retention window.
provisions.risk_framework: 2.2 E-SIGN, TCPA, Reg P and Reg F; UDAAP communications

provisions.family_title: Consumer notices, electronic consent and communications
provisions.title: Debt-collection contact frequency stays inside the presumptive seven-calls-in-seven-days limit and the seven-day post-conversation limit, a cease request stops the channel, and validation information precedes collection activity
provisions.citation: FDCPA, 15 U.S.C. §1692c and §1692d; Reg. F, 12 CFR §1006.14(b)(2)(i)-(ii) (presumptive contact-frequency limits) and §1006.34 (validation information)
provisions.source_status: US statute and regulation, public domain. Ordinary because §1006.14(b)(2) sets a rebuttable presumption rather than a flat prohibition, so a documented exception can exist — which is exactly the distinction Definition 1 turns on.
provisions.risk_framework: 2.2 E-SIGN, TCPA, Reg P and Reg F; UDAAP communications

provisions.family_title: Deposit fees, funds availability and account handling
provisions.title: Deposit account fees, the annual percentage yield and its computation method are disclosed before the account is opened, and a change in terms that reduces the yield or adds a fee is noticed before it takes effect
provisions.citation: Truth in Savings Act, 12 U.S.C. §4301 et seq.; Reg. DD, 12 CFR §§1030.4 (account disclosures), 1030.5 (change-in-terms notice) and 1030.11 (advertising the annual percentage yield)
provisions.source_status: US statute and regulation, public domain. Ordinary: Reg. DD prescribes content and timing, and a late or incomplete disclosure is curable, so a risk owner can meaningfully accept a residual here.
provisions.risk_framework: 2.2 Reg DD, Reg E overdraft, Reg CC; state unclaimed-property law

provisions.family_title: Deposit fees, funds availability and account handling
provisions.title: No fee is assessed for paying an ATM or one-time debit card overdraft unless the consumer's affirmative opt-in is recorded first, and the service defaults to declining the transaction until it is
provisions.citation: Reg. E, 12 CFR §1005.17(b) (affirmative consent before assessing an overdraft fee on an ATM or one-time debit card transaction) and §1005.17(d) (segregated notice content)
provisions.source_status: US regulation, public domain. Absolute because §1005.17(b) makes the consumer's own affirmative consent the condition precedent: only the consumer may supply it, so no officer of the firm — however senior — is competent to decide the fee may be charged without it. That is Definition 1's who-may-decide test, not a claim about severity.
provisions.risk_framework: 2.2 Reg DD, Reg E overdraft, Reg CC; state unclaimed-property law

provisions.family_title: Deposit fees, funds availability and account handling
provisions.title: The funds-availability schedule, including next-business-day availability and the exception holds that may extend it, is read from the regulated table and is never lengthened, tuned or defaulted by a service setting
provisions.citation: Expedited Funds Availability Act, 12 U.S.C. §4001 et seq.; Reg. CC, 12 CFR §§229.10, 229.12, 229.13 (exceptions) and 229.13(g) (exception notice)
provisions.source_status: US statute and regulation, public domain. Absolute because the schedule and the permitted exceptions are fixed by the regulation and its dollar amounts are set by the Bureau's inflation adjustments; a firm that lengthens a hold is legislating. The current adjusted dollar thresholds are directionally supported, not verified as of 6 September 2026, which is why the provision binds to the regulated table rather than to a number.
provisions.risk_framework: 2.2 Reg DD, Reg E overdraft, Reg CC; state unclaimed-property law

provisions.family_title: Deposit fees, funds availability and account handling
provisions.title: Dormancy periods, owner due-diligence notices and remittance deadlines are read from the governing state's unclaimed-property table, and no internal system event resets an account's dormancy clock
provisions.citation: State unclaimed-property acts, most of them variants of the Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act (2016) model; priority rules from Texas v. New Jersey, 379 U.S. 674 (1965)
provisions.source_status: State statutes are edicts of government; the RUUPA model is cited by identifier. There is no federal escheat statute — say so rather than imply one: escheat is entirely a matter of state law, which is why the provision binds to a jurisdiction table and is ordinary rather than absolute. Periods and due-diligence thresholds differ state by state and are directionally supported, not verified state by state.
provisions.risk_framework: 2.2 Reg DD, Reg E overdraft, Reg CC; state unclaimed-property law

provisions.family_title: Military, servicemember and vulnerable-customer protections
provisions.title: Covered-borrower status is determined before consummation, the military annual percentage rate stays at or below thirty-six per cent with every included charge counted, and the prohibited terms are refused
provisions.citation: Military Lending Act, 10 U.S.C. §987; 32 CFR §§232.3 (military annual percentage rate), 232.4 (the thirty-six per cent limit and prohibited terms), 232.5 (covered-borrower identification and safe harbour) and 232.6 (oral and written disclosures)
provisions.source_status: US statute and regulation, public domain. Absolute because §987(f)(3) makes a credit agreement that violates the section void from inception — a consequence Congress attached to the transaction itself, which no risk owner can accept away.
provisions.risk_framework: 2.2 MLA and SCRA; elder financial exploitation

provisions.family_title: Military, servicemember and vulnerable-customer protections
provisions.title: On valid notice of military service the interest rate on a pre-service obligation is reduced to six per cent with the excess forgiven, and no repossession or foreclosure of protected property proceeds without a court order
provisions.citation: Servicemembers Civil Relief Act, 50 U.S.C. §3937 (six per cent maximum rate, excess interest forgiven), §3952 (instalment contracts: no rescission or repossession without a court order) and §3953 (mortgages and trust deeds)
provisions.source_status: US statute, public domain. Absolute because §3952 and §3953 reserve the decision to a court: the relief is granted or withheld by a judge, not by the creditor, and §3937 forgives rather than defers the excess. A firm officer who overrides either is exercising a power the statute placed elsewhere.
provisions.risk_framework: 2.2 MLA and SCRA; elder financial exploitation

provisions.family_title: Military, servicemember and vulnerable-customer protections
provisions.title: The path by which suspected financial exploitation of an older or vulnerable customer is escalated, held where state law permits, and reported stays reachable from the servicing case and is never downgraded to a passive report
provisions.citation: Senior Safe Act, Pub. L. 115-174 §303 (2018), 12 U.S.C. §3423 (immunity for trained employees of a covered financial institution); FinCEN Advisory FIN-2022-A002, Elder Financial Exploitation (15 June 2022); state mandatory-reporting statutes (e.g. Cal. Welf. & Inst. Code §15630.1)
provisions.source_status: US statute and FinCEN advisory are public domain; state statutes are edicts of government. Ordinary rather than absolute: the federal instrument grants immunity for reporting rather than compelling it, and whether reporting is mandatory varies by state, so the software floor is that the path exists and is confidential either way.
provisions.risk_framework: 2.2 MLA and SCRA; elder financial exploitation

provisions.family_title: Data-subject rights, opt-out signals and accessibility
provisions.title: A data-subject access request is answered within one month and a portability request produces a structured, commonly used, machine-readable export; an extension is notified with its reasons rather than taken silently
provisions.citation: GDPR, Reg. (EU) 2016/679 Arts. 15 (access) and 20 (portability), with the deadline and the two-month extension at Art. 12(3)
provisions.source_status: EU text reusable under Decision 2011/833/EU. Ordinary because Art. 12(3) itself contemplates an extension for complex requests, so the period is a bounded discretion rather than a fixed floor; the existing MF-105 and MF-558 carry the transfer and erasure duties.
provisions.risk_framework: 2.1 GDPR access and portability; CPRA opt-out signals; accessibility floor

provisions.family_title: Data-subject rights, opt-out signals and accessibility
provisions.title: Customer-facing surfaces carry an accessibility regression gate at WCAG 2.2 Level AA in the release pipeline, and a Level A or AA failure blocks the release rather than being downgraded to a warning
provisions.citation: ADA Title III, 42 U.S.C. §12182 and 28 CFR Part 36; WCAG 2.2 (W3C Recommendation, 5 October 2023), Level AA, cited by identifier; European Accessibility Act, Dir. (EU) 2019/882, applicable from 28 June 2025, whose Annex I covers consumer banking services
provisions.source_status: US statute and regulation public domain; EU text reusable; W3C material cited by identifier only. Note the DOJ web-accessibility rule of 2024 sits at 28 CFR Part 35 and binds Title II public entities only, so a private firm's WCAG 2.2 AA target rests on Title III case law and, in the EU, on the EAA — which is why this is ordinary rather than absolute.
provisions.risk_framework: 2.1 GDPR access and portability; CPRA opt-out signals; accessibility floor

provisions.family_title: Data-subject rights, opt-out signals and accessibility
provisions.title: An opt-out preference signal is detected and treated as a valid request to stop sale and sharing without any further prompt, and is linked to the known customer record where one exists
provisions.citation: CCPA/CPRA, Cal. Civ. Code §1798.135(b); California Privacy Protection Agency regulations, 11 CCR §7025 (opt-out preference signals)
provisions.source_status: California statute and regulations are edicts of government. Ordinary and deliberately narrower than MF-404, which states the substantive opt-out duty: this provision governs the automated signal specifically, so a change that ignores the header is charged here rather than competing with MF-404.
provisions.risk_framework: 2.1 GDPR access and portability; CPRA opt-out signals; accessibility floor

provisions.family_title: Virtual assets and the breadth of the financial-crime programme
provisions.title: A transfer involving convertible virtual currency carries the originator and beneficiary records the rule requires, the counterparty wallet provider is identified beforehand, and an unhosted-wallet transfer is recorded with the declared evidence
provisions.citation: 31 CFR §1010.410(f) (the Travel Rule) read with §1010.410(e) (recordkeeping) and FinCEN Guidance FIN-2019-G001 treating convertible virtual currency as 'funds'; FATF Recommendation 16
provisions.source_status: US regulation and FinCEN guidance, public domain; FATF material CC BY 4.0. Absolute because the transmittal-of-records duty attaches to the transfer itself with strict liability under 31 U.S.C. §5318(a)(2), and only FinCEN may set the threshold. Note the overlap with MF-524, which states the same duty for funds transfers generally — filed as PA-08 rather than resolved here.
provisions.risk_framework: 2.2 Travel Rule, currency transaction reporting, 314(a), PEP and EDD

provisions.family_title: Virtual assets and the breadth of the financial-crime programme
provisions.title: Currency transactions above the reporting threshold are aggregated across the business day and reported within the statutory window; no threshold setting, exemption flag or batch schedule suppresses or defers a filing
provisions.citation: 31 U.S.C. §5313; 31 CFR §1010.311 (reports of transactions in currency), §1010.306(a)(1) (filing within fifteen days), §1010.313 (aggregation) and §1010.315 (exemptions); structuring prohibited by 31 U.S.C. §5324
provisions.source_status: US statute and regulation, public domain. Absolute because the filing duty and its threshold are set by statute and regulation, the failure to file is itself the offence, and assisting a customer to fall below the threshold is separately criminal under §5324 — none of which any officer of the firm may accept as a residual risk.
provisions.risk_framework: 2.2 Travel Rule, currency transaction reporting, 314(a), PEP and EDD

provisions.family_title: Virtual assets and the breadth of the financial-crime programme
provisions.title: Information requests from the financial-intelligence unit are matched across every account system and retained, and politically exposed person screening and enhanced due diligence run before a relationship opens and again on the declared refresh cycle
provisions.citation: 31 CFR §1010.520 (information sharing between government agencies and financial institutions, the fourteen-day search); §1010.610 (correspondent account due diligence); FFIEC BSA/AML Examination Manual, politically exposed persons and enhanced due diligence sections (title cited as a fact)
provisions.source_status: US regulation, public domain; the FFIEC manual is cited by title with no text reproduced. Ordinary because there is no US rule that defines a politically exposed person or mandates a specific screening design — the expectation is supervisory, so this is a firm control informed by the manual rather than a restatement of a rule.
